title: Finance Business Partner - Energy Transition Finance Team
description: Location: Copenhagen, Denmark At Maersk, we're working to enable the transition towards net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2040. New fuels, evolving regulations, and changing customer expectations are reshaping our industry, and our Energy Transition team is at the heart of that transformation. We're looking for a Finance Business Partner to join our Energy Transition Finance team and help support the financial decisions that will shape the future of sustainable shipping. This is not a traditional finance partnering role. You'll work at the intersection of finance, energy markets, green fuels, regulation, and business transformation, partnering with stakeholders across our commercial, trading, origination, operational, and finance communities. What you'll be doing In this role, you'll provide financial insights and decision support across Maersk's green fuel activities. You'll help evaluate opportunities, assess risks, and ensure we make informed decisions as we scale our decarbonization efforts. Your responsibilities will include: Driving performance management, reporting, forecasting, and planning activities Conducting financial, scenario, and sensitivity analyses to support business decisions Supporting financial due diligence for fuel supply agreements and new products Helping stakeholders understand the financial implications of evolving fuel markets and regulations Identifying opportunities to improve reporting, processes, and automation Building strong partnerships across Energy Transition, Energy Markets, and Finance teams Supporting the development of sustainable financial processes for emerging fuels and regulatory requirements Who we're looking for We're seeking someone with strong analytical and business partnering skills, combined with a genuine interest in the energy transition landscape. You may already have experience within energy, fuels, commodities, trading, renewables, sustainability, or a related sector. Equally, you may bring strong finance experience and a track record of quickly building expertise in complex and evolving subject areas. We're particularly interested in candidates who bring: Experience in finance business partnering, commercial finance, FP&A, product control, risk, or a similar analytical role Strong financial modelling and analytical capabilities Experience working with data and tools such as Excel and Power BI The ability to communicate complex topics clearly and influence a diverse range of stakeholders A proactive, curious, and solutions-oriented mindset Comfort navigating ambiguity and solving problems in a fast-changing environment ** Experience within energy markets, fuels, commodities, decarbonization, sustainability, or related industries will be a significant advantage. Why join us? This is a unique opportunity to work on one of Maersk's most strategic priorities and contribute to the decarbonization of global trade. You'll gain exposure to complex commercial decisions, emerging fuel markets, evolving regulation, and senior business stakeholders, while developing expertise in an area that is shaping the future of our industry. Ready to help drive the energy transition? We'd love to hear from you. Even if you don't meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply if you're excited about the opportunity and believe you can bring valuable experience, curiosity, and perspective to the team. title: Collections and Recovery Specialist at Volvo Financial Services (Vilnius or Riga)
description: Transport is at the core of modern society. Imagine using your expertise to shape sustainable transport and infrastructure solutions for the future. If you seek to make a difference on a global scale, working with next-gen technologies and the sharpest collaborative teams, then we could be a perfect match. What you will do At Volvo Financial Services you will contribute to the transformation of our company, the transport industry and society at large. The Collections & Recovery Specialist plays an important role in supporting portfolio quality and minimizing credit losses across Lithuania, Latvia, and Estonia. The role combines analytical, operational and decision-support responsibilities by monitoring collections performance, preparing portfolio and overdue debt reporting, reviewing contract modification requests, and providing recommendations to support sound credit and collections decisions. The position reports to the Credit Manager at Volvo Financial Services Baltics. Main activities and core responsibilities: • Monitor collections and recovery performance across the Baltic portfolio. • Work with soft collections providers and directly with customers, as needed, to determine cause of delinquency and negotiate payment arrangements. • Prepare and maintain overdue debt (OVD), delinquency and collections performance reports for management. • Ensure data quality and consistency within collections and portfolio management reporting. • Analyze portfolio trends, identify risk areas and recommend corrective actions. • Review customer requests for contract modifications, payment extensions and restructurings. • Perform financial and risk assessment of modification requests and prepare recommendations for approval. • Initiate and handle termination of contracts due to default. • Coordinate Repossession and support Remarketing functions as required. • Support decision-making by providing portfolio, collections and recovery insights. • Monitor recovery performance and support actions aimed at maximizing recovered amounts. • Lead periodic collection meetings to discuss individual accounts and action items. • Drive continuous improvements in collections, recovery and contract administration processes. • Support implementation of new tools, products and business initiatives impacting collections activities. Who are you? In this role, you will bring: • University degree in Finance, Economics, Business Administration or a related field. • Minimum 3 years of experience in collections, credit, risk management, accounts receivables or financial analysis. Experience in a customer service or similar environment is an advantage. • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. • Ability to assess financial risks and identify appropriate mitigation actions. • Good understanding of leasing and loan products. • High attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities. • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills. • Experience working in an international and multicultural environment is an advantage. • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, particularly Excel. • Fluency in Lithuanian or Latvian and advanced level of English. What’s in it for you? We offer a solid package of compensation and benefits, plus you will enjoy: • Joining a global and diverse team of highly skilled professionals who make customers win. • Opportunity to grow both personally and professionally. • Space to initiate and implement improvements that create value for customers and the business. • Environment where we work with passion, trust each other and embrace change to stay ahead. • Package of company benefits such as trainings, additional health insurance and more. Salary level: from 2.900€ to 3.600€ per month gross (before withholding taxes) depending on skills and experience. Also, annual bonus program will be applied in accordance with the Company policy. Ready for the next move? If you are a proactive professional with strong analytical capabilities, customer focus and integrity, we would like to meet you. Apply now to join Volvo Financial Services Baltics and help us maintain a healthy portfolio while delivering excellent customer support and sustainable business results. For further information, please contact: Vilma Suchockiene, People & Culture Manager Mob. +370 686 77016; email: vilma.suchockiene@volvo.com We value your data privacy and therefore do not accept applications via mail. title: Market Risk Analyst
description: We are seeking talented professionals to join our Risk Management team. The market risk team plays a central role in analysing, measuring, managing, and communicating the risks associated with the Asset and Origination portfolios, including related hedging strategies. The team is also responsible for independent analysis and for supporting the implementation of new contracts in our risk systems. Regularly report on the performance (P&L) and risks associated with our Asset and Origination portfolios, providing accurate and timely information to stakeholders. Monitor energy market developments, regulatory changes, and their potential impact on our portfolios. Perform comprehensive risk assessments of transactions and deal structures before execution, identifying key risks and proposing appropriate mitigation measures. Collaborate with internal stakeholders, including originators, portfolio managers, analysts, and credit risk teams, to ensure robust risk management and deal viability. Contribute to the continuous improvement of risk management processes and tools by sharing insights and proposing enhancements. We look for a Market Risk Analyst with the skills to future-proof our business and strengthen our market risk team. That includes: Advanced university degree in a quantitative discipline like Finance, Mathematics, Statistics, Physics, Economics, Engineering or equivalent discipline. Knowledge of valuing and modelling derivatives is preferred. Programming experience (Preferably in Python). Strong attention to detail, integrity, and a proactive team player. Excellent communication skills with the ability to confidently engage with stakeholders. Fluent in English, both written and spoken. Knowledge of Norwegian is an advantage but not required This position is suitable for candidates with prior experience in energy markets or risk management, as well as talented graduates with an interest in renewable energy markets.

title: PreMaster-Programm – Managementassistenz im FC-Bereich, Schwerpunkt Controlling (w/m/div.)
description: In dieser Position übernehmen Sie die Verantwortung für die Überwachung der geschäftlichen und finanziellen Aspekte der von Ihrem Team vorgeschlagenen Kosteneinsparungsmaßnahmen. Durch Ihr Verständnis des finanziellen Hintergrunds dieser Veränderungen spielen Sie eine wichtige Rolle bei der Bewertung des Fortschritts dieser Maßnahmen. Dies erfolgt durch die Analyse der erwarteten Ergebnisse sowie des kommerziellen Status dieser Veränderungen. Bei diesen Aufgaben werden Sie von verschiedenen Teams weltweit unterstützt (Deutschland, Ungarn, Rumänien, USA, Indien und Mexiko). Sie stehen dabei nicht nur in engem Austausch mit Controlling-Teams, sondern auch mit den Bereichen Einkauf, Vertrieb und vielen weiteren Bosch-Einheiten weltweit. Gemeinsam stellen Sie entscheidungsrelevante Finanzinformationen bereit, die für Managemententscheidungen und die Projektsteuerung genutzt werden – insbesondere in Zusammenarbeit mit dem Controlling-Team bei der Erstellung der monatlichen Management-Reports. Ausbildung: Sie müssen ein Bachelorstudium in den Bereichen Statistik, Management, Informatik oder Wirtschaftswissenschaften erfolgreich abgeschlossen haben, dabei deutlich überdurchschnittliche Leistungen erzielt haben und fest beabsichtigen, anschließend ein Masterstudium aufzunehmen. Erfahrung und Kenntnisse: Sie verfügen idealerweise über einen Hintergrund in Datenanalyse sowie Planung & Forecasting. Projektmanagement-Erfahrung ist von Vorteil. Zudem bringen Sie sehr gute Kenntnisse in Excel, PowerPoint und Power BI mit. Qualifikationen: Sie sind gut organisiert, teamorientiert, kommunikativ und international ausgerichtet. Sprachen: Englisch auf C1-Niveau ist erforderlich, Deutsch auf B1-Niveau ist von Vorteil.
description_en: In this position, you will be responsible for overseeing the business and financial aspects of your team's proposed cost savings measures. By understanding the financial background of these changes, you will play an important role in assessing the progress of these measures. This is done by analyzing the expected results as well as the commercial status of these changes. You will be supported in these tasks by various teams around the world (Germany, Hungary, Romania, USA, India and Mexico). You are not only in close contact with controlling teams, but also with purchasing, sales and many other Bosch units worldwide. Together, you will provide decision-relevant financial information that is used for management decisions and project control - especially in collaboration with the controlling team when preparing the monthly management reports. Education: You must have successfully completed a bachelor's degree in the fields of statistics, management, computer science or economics, have achieved significantly above-average performance and firmly intend to subsequently take up a master's degree. Experience and knowledge: Ideally, you have a background in data analysis and planning & forecasting. Project management experience is an advantage. You also have very good knowledge of Excel, PowerPoint and Power BI.

The ideal candidate will have at least 10 years of relevant experience as a trader or risk manager specializing in the trading of physical oil products at a reputable physical commodities trading house. This role requires an in-depth understanding of physical oil markets, pricing mechanisms, logistics, quality and blending, regulations, market dynamics, contractual terms, and market participants. description: Transport vormt de kern van onze moderne samenleving. Stel je voor dat je jouw expertise kan toepassen om duurzame transport- en infrastructureoplossingen voor de toekomst vorm te geven. Het vervullen van onze missie creëert ontelbare carrièremogelijkheden voor talenten binnen de toonaangevende merken en entiteiten van de groep. We zijn gepassioneerd over wat we doen en gedijen op teamwork. We zijn bijna 100.000 mensen die wereldwijd verenigd zijn door een cultuur van zorg, inclusiviteit en empowerment. De divisie Trucks Technology & Industrial neemt teamspelers aan die klaar zijn om echte impact te maken voor onze klanten. Onze gedecentraliseerde teams werken dicht bij onze klanten, met snelheid en autonomie, om te bouwen wat zij echt nodig hebben.Sluit je bij ons aan om samen te werken aan innovatieve, duurzame technologieën die opnieuw definiëren hoe wij waarde ontwerpen, bouwen en leveren. Breng je nieuwsgierigheid, je expertise en je samenwerkingskracht mee en samen zullen we gedurfde ideeën omzetten in tastbare oplossingen voor onze klanten en bijdragen aan een duurzamere toekomst.

description_en: Working in Origination – New Business & Portfolio Management As part of Statkraft's front office, the Central European Origination team completes non-standard, structured and often complex transactions in the wholesale energy markets and provides market access services. Working closely with Statkraft's commercial department and the other regional origination teams, we develop tailored energy solutions for customers across Europe. The areas of responsibility within the team are divided into origination, new business, direct marketing and portfolio management. In the origination area, we are responsible for the development of tailor-made solutions and products for our contractual partners (upstream/downstream) - from development to economic analysis, negotiation, contract drafting and contract conclusion through to implementation. The “New Business” team focuses on the development of new, economically successful structured products that complement established sustainability solutions with flexibility. A central topic is battery storage marketing and related products. Portfolio management is divided into two teams. Through continuous innovation and a dedicated focus on scientific and technical excellence, we strive to develop and launch new, groundbreaking treatments that address critical health challenges. This role incumbent leads and manages the end to end expense planning processes across Global Specialty GPS & Medical (budget of ~£180m) and has specific responsibility to partner early pipeline Commercial and Medical Portfolio teams. In this role you will: End to End expense management responsibilities: Along with ad-hoc analysis and project involvement, the key responsibilities of the role will include: Partnering with the Portfolio teams (Commercial Ops & Strategy and Portfolio strategy) teams (~£21m budget responsibility), including monthly meetings with team leads to provide financial management of variance to budget. Providing financial management for the Specialty Care expenditure, including driving the Plan/LQE/MYE/FC1 setting process and the consolidation. Providing monthly commentary for achieving Plan/MYE/FC1/LQE highlighting key gaps and questions on Headcount, Variable Spend and Evidence Generation. Support FP and VP in overall financial control of expense budgets, taking direction to work up options to reallocate funding to areas of greatest need Design and distribute monthly reports to Specialty Care including flash sales report, flash sales commentary, expenditure reports and summary portfolio deck. Prepare deck for Specialty Care Leadership Team on monthly performance to focus leaders on key drivers of the business. Keeping the headcount tracker up to date and working with HR, finance partners to make any changes. Support FP and VP in financial control of headcount costs, explaining assumptions, deviations from plan and options to close gaps Working cross functionally with the medical team, manage the financial process within the data generation planning process in preparation for the annual Medical Review Board for decision making on funding for new data generation studies. Working with the KC and other Finance Partners to ensure all month end activities and reports are delivered on time, efficiently and effectively. Manage submissions into key processes and systems e.g. SAC Ad hoc Sales and Profitability analysis, including developing insights and presentations for senior management. Early pipeline finance partnering responsibilities: Manage headcount, variable and evidence generation expenditure budgets partnering with the commercial and medical teams. Drive strategic discussions with the teams to understand the pipeline stages, governance timelines and plan for resourcing the assets for success. Evaluate the risk profile and recommend resourcing to VP Finance Educate and influence business partners to plan over a longer time horizon to prepare the organisation for the evolution of the portfolio. Why you? Basic Qualifications : We are looking for professionals with these required skills to achieve our goals: Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Business, Economics etc. or equivalent experience CIMA/Other Professional Accounting Qualifications Good experience in Finance or budget management roles Significant experience with senior stakeholder engagement, including up to VP level Preferred Skills : If you have the following characteristics, it would be a plus: Experience applying financial analysis to support business decisions, including evaluation of risks, investment options, and trade-offs. Ability to work across time zones (US, UK and Europe) Good knowledge of GSK Finance standards, systems and processes. Demonstrated ability to apply strategic thinking, solve complex problems and influence decisions in a matrix organisation. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build credibility, challenge constructively and collaborate effectively across diverse teams. description: Transport is at the core of modern society. Imagine using your expertise to shape sustainable transport and infrastructure solutions for the future. If you seek to make a difference on a global scale, working with next-gen technologies and the sharpest collaborative teams, then we could be a perfect match. What you will do As Head of Finance you will lead and develop a team of highly competent, engaged, and passionate finance professionals supporting Volvo CE's strategic component operation in Eskilstuna. This is a senior leadership role where you act as a trusted business partner to the organization, combining strong financial expertise with a deep understanding of manufacturing performance and long-term value creation. You have full responsibility for the financial agenda of the site, ensuring sound financial governance while supporting strategic and operational decision-making. You play a critical role in securing profitability, evaluating investments, driving performance improvements, and translating business strategies into measurable results. The role requires a strong foundation in traditional finance and controlling disciplines, including financial planning, forecasting, cost management, investment analysis, business case development, and performance management. At the same time, you will operate in a Lean and Volvo Production System (VPS) environment, where financial insights must be closely integrated with operational excellence and continuous improvement. You and your team will also play a key role in supporting the site's strategy deployment process, ensuring that financial objectives, operational priorities, and strategic ambitions are connected and translated into actionable plans throughout the organization. Reporting to the Head of Operations & Site Eskilstuna, Robert Kusén, you will contribute to Volvo CE's strategy, “Building Tomorrow Together”. Eskilstuna is a key strategic site within Volvo CE, supplying facilities globally with a great Technology footprint, driving the development of future machines, systems and digital solutions. Who are you? We are looking for a senior, business-driven finance leader with a passion for manufacturing, performance improvement, and people development. Most importantly, you bring a strong background in finance and financial leadership. You understand the fundamentals of financial management and know how to leverage financial insights to influence business decisions, improve operational performance, and drive profitable growth. Previous work experience from lean, operational excellence, or similar environments is also required. You understand how financial performance is created on the shop floor and how finance can support strategy execution through structured performance management and strategy deployment. You are comfortable operating at both strategic and operational levels, partnering with senior leaders while remaining close to the business. You build credibility through strong financial acumen, commercial understanding, and personal integrity. As a leader, you create engagement, develop capability, and build high-performing teams that deliver results while living Volvo Group's values. To succeed in this role, you should have: University degree in Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or equivalent. Extensive experience in senior finance leadership roles within manufacturing or industrial operations. Strong expertise in financial planning, controlling, investment analysis, costing, profitability management, and business performance management. Proven ability to act as a strategic business partner and influence decision-making at senior management level. Demonstrated experience from manufacturing environments with a strong understanding of operational drivers and value creation. Experience working with lean, strategy deployment, operational excellence, or similar business systems. Strong leadership experience with a proven track record of developing teams and driving organizational performance. Fluent in Swedish and English, both spoken and written. Are we a perfect match? We can't promise you an effortless job, but we can promise talented colleagues, significant business impact, and exciting challenges. This is an opportunity to lead the finance agenda at one of Volvo CE's most important sites. You will have a central role in driving profitability, supporting strategic investments, and ensuring that financial and operational performance go hand in hand.

title: Finance Portfolio Analytics Manager
description: At GSK we unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. Deciding which R&D projects to invest in — and how to sequence, resource and prioritise them — is one of the most consequential judgements we make. The Portfolio Data Science team turns scientific, clinical, operational and financial inputs into the analysis and insight that guide those investment decisions across short-, medium- and long-range horizons. Position Summary Reporting to the Head, Data Science, Analytics, and AI, the Finance Portfolio Analytics Manager builds and leads the analytical capability that underpins R&D portfolio and investment decision-making. You will design the models, frameworks and dashboards the team relies on, and lead ad hoc strategic analyses that answer complex, high-stakes portfolio questions — translating scientific and clinical information into quantified investment and financial impact. This is a senior individual-contributor role. You will not have direct reports, but you will act as the analytical lead for portfolio analytics — setting standards, guiding and mentoring analysts, and being the trusted partner senior stakeholders turn to for rigorous, decision-ready analysis. Key Responsibilities Analytics capability & methodology – Design, build and own the portfolio analytics toolkit — valuation models (NPV/rNPV), scenario and sensitivity analysis, probabilistic and Monte Carlo simulation, and portfolio optimisation and prioritisation approaches. – Establish reusable, well-documented models, templates and standards so that analyses are transparent, reproducible and auditable. – Continuously improve forecasting methodologies, data quality, and reporting and analytics tooling. Strategic & ad hoc analysis – Lead ad hoc strategic analyses to address complex, ambiguous investment and portfolio questions, defining the problem statement where only limited framing exists. – Develop, evaluate and stress-test business cases, valuations and investment scenarios. – Translate scientific, clinical and operational inputs into quantified financial and investment impact. Portfolio performance & forecasting – Build and maintain portfolio forecasts across annual, multi-year and long-range planning horizons. – Define and track portfolio metrics, milestones and KPIs; monitor performance against plan and surface variances and risks with recommended actions. – Support investment allocation and budget phasing aligned to portfolio priorities. Decision support & governance – Prepare insights, materials and recommendations for portfolio and product review discussions and investment governance cycles. – Present trade-offs, risks and financial impact to senior leadership, and influence decisions through structured, data-backed recommendations. – Consolidate inputs from scientific, clinical, regulatory, commercial, finance and technology stakeholders into a coherent portfolio view. Collaboration & enablement – Partner across development, operations, finance and technology teams to align on assumptions, data and methods. – Set analytical standards and mentor and guide analysts; champion best practice and the responsible use of Gen AI and advanced analytics to accelerate and strengthen analysis. Basic Qualifications – Bachelor’s degree in a quantitative field (engineering, computer science, mathematics, economics, operations research, finance ) or life sciences with specific quantitative experience. – Demonstrated experience in financial & operational modelling, valuation, investment analysis, decision science or a related area field. – Demonstrated expertise translating data science insights into actionable recommendations. – Experience defining problem statements from limited initial information and managing multiple parallel priorities to agreed timelines. – Experience preparing and presenting executive-level analysis and influencing decisions through structured communication and data-backed recommendations. – Proficiency with least one analytical or programming language (e.g. Python or R), together with exposure to data science app development frameworks (Shiny, Streamlit, Dash etc.) Preferred Qualifications – Advanced degree (MBA, MSc or equivalent) in a finance, quantitative, scientific or business discipline. – Direct exposure to drug development and R&D portfolio or investment decision-making in pharmaceutical, biotech or a related industry. – Strong data science fundamentals with particular exposure to Monte Carlo modellin

title: Senior OT Network & Systems Engineer - Battery Energy Storage Systems - Volvo Energy
description: Transport is at the core of modern society. Imagine using your expertise to shape sustainable transport and infrastructure solutions for the future. If you seek to make a difference on a global scale, working with next-gen technologies and the sharpest collaborative teams, then we could be a perfect match. Working at Volvo Energy is different Do you want to make the world a better place and love architecting digital solutions? Welcome to a team unified by an important mission, great ideas, fun, diversity, and inclusiveness. Our colleagues are - and will always be - the most important part of the story. Whilst demands are high, there is also plenty of opportunities to learn and grow - as a professional and as a person. We look for colleagues that thoroughly enjoy our intrapreneurial journey, can hit the ground running and lead with passion, perform with purpose and transform with vision. Moreover, it will be essential you have a strong ability to form trustful relationships to effectively work with partners - inside and outside of the Volvo Group – in a cross-functional manner. You will make a difference! Volvo Energy Digital & IT Digital & IT is a function within Volvo Energy. We support our customers transition to a carbon-free world through great Digital solutions and experiences that users love and enables customers to shift to fossil-free operations. We truly care about the customer’s business in terms of up-time, safety, productivity and of course 100% green energy supply. We aim at having industry-leading simplicity and usability for our digital services, such as routing, find-book-pay and charging operator systems. The energy transition will not come for free – but we are committed to support this transition by hard and dedicated work. So - what are we looking for in this specific role? Volvo Energy is providing a highly qualified digital platform, an Energy Management System (EMS), to control our Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). We are now looking for Senior OT Network & Systems Engineer that will support in establishing cyber secure connectivity towards BESS units and the BESS digital twin using the appointed Volvo Energy Site Controller. As the energy space rely on standards for interoperability between energy systems, like Modbus, IEC 60870-5, 61850 and DNP-3, you make sure that the IoT Edge solution is designed according to cyber security standards. You also ensure cyber secure connectivity to the Volvo Energy EMS solution via MQTT/OPC-UA as defined by the Volvo Energy target architecture. You will work closely together with several different qualified teams to help design and build the solution and report functionally to the Volvo Energy Head of Enterprise architecture. Key Responsibilities In this role, you’ll take the lead in shaping the OT network architecture that powers our BESS units around the world. You’ll design secure, scalable network environments—everything from segmentation and VLAN structures to DMZ zones and redundancy strategies—both for our own products and for customer sites. As the technical owner of our OT networking landscape, you’ll create and maintain clear, high‑quality diagrams and documentation that bring structure to complex systems and ensure smooth integration with cloud platforms and external SCADA/EMS solutions. A big part of your work will center around cybersecurity. You’ll define modern firewall rulesets built on IEC 62443 and zero‑trust principles, validate safe communication paths for industrial protocols like Modbus, and take full responsibility for the lifecycle of our OT firewalls. That includes firmware updates, patching strategies, redundancy testing, vendor coordination, and the automated deployment of configurations across our global BESS fleet using FortiManager. You’ll also play a hands-on role in our production environments—diving into troubleshooting, leading root‑cause analysis, and contributing to cybersecurity assessments and audits that strengthen our defenses. Collaboration will be at the heart of your everyday work. You’ll partner with engineering teams at our assembly plants to ensure firewalls are configured correctly from the moment a unit is built, and you’ll work with Digital/IT teams to define secure, future‑proof IT–OT demarcation points. Along the way, you’ll also share your expertise with junior engineers and project teams, helping them grow while raising the overall technical bar. Required Qualifications 7+ years in OT networking, indus

title: Business Controller
description: Do you enjoy driving business performance from a central finance position? Are you an experienced finance professional who can turn complex financial data into strategic insights? Do you thrive in a role where you oversee the bigger picture, steer reporting processes, and support senior management with decision-making? We are looking for a Business Controller to join the Business Control team within Vattenfall's rapidly growing E-Mobility Business Unit. In this central controlling role, you will be responsible for providing insights into the overall financial performance of the Business Unit. You will act as a key partner to senior management, ensuring high-quality financial reporting, forecasting, planning, and performance steering across multiple countries and business areas. Working closely with Business Control colleagues, Finance teams, and senior stakeholders, you will help translate financial results into actionable insights that support the continued growth and development of Vattenfall's E-Mobility business. What will you do? As Senior Business Controller, you will play a key role in steering the overall financial performance of the E-Mobility Business Unit and ensuring a reliable and efficient reporting framework. You will: Coordinate and steer the monthly performance reporting cycle for the overall Business Unit. Consolidate financial results across countries, functions, and business areas into clear management reporting. Deliver insights and analyses on business performance, key value drivers, risks, and opportunities. Lead forecasting activities and translate business developments into reliable financial outlooks. Drive the annual budget and business planning process for the Business Unit. Support senior management with strategic analyses, business cases, and decision-making. Further develop and improve reporting standards, controlling processes, and governance frameworks. Ensure consistency, accuracy, and transparency in financial reporting and performance measurement. Collaborate closely with Business Controllers, Accounting, and Finance teams across different countries. Identify opportunities to automate and enhance reporting tools, KPIs, and management information. Contribute to cross-functional improvement initiatives that support the continued growth of E-Mobility. You will report to the Director of Business Control E-Mobility and work closely with stakeholders across multiple countries and disciplines. Who are you? You are able to combine strong analytical capabilities with a strategic mindset and enjoy understanding how financial performance connects to broader business objectives. You are comfortable working with large amounts of data, creating structure in complex environments, and translating financial outcomes into meaningful insights for senior stakeholders. You can switch effortlessly between detailed financial analysis and high-level performance discussions. With a proactive and collaborative approach, you build strong relationships across the organisation and contribute to continuous improvement. We believe you bring: At least 7 years of experience in Business Controlling, Financial Controlling, FP&A, Corporate Finance, or a similar finance-related role. A master's degree in Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field. Experience with consolidated reporting, forecasting, and business planning in a complex international organisation. Strong analytical and financial modelling skills. Experience working with senior stakeholders and management teams. The ability to translate complex financial information into clear and actionable recommendations. Advanced Excel and presentation skills; experience with SAP and reporting tools is highly valued. Full professional proficiency in English. Experience within the utilities, energy, infrastructure, or other asset-intensive industries is considered an advantage. Location: Berlin, Stockholm or Amsterdam

title: Director Analytics Infrastructure, Pipeline Operations
description: Job Description Summary #LI- Remote Novartis has an exciting opportunity for a Director, Analytics Infrastructure & Pipeline Operations. This role is responsible for building next-generation, AI-powered automated data pipelines and scalable data repositories that enable enterprise data science and analytics at scale. By leveraging advanced AI technologies, modern data engineering tools, and feature engineering platforms, this director creates self-service, analytics-ready datasets and enterprise feature stores that empower both expert data scientists and citizen data scientists to rapidly develop, deploy, and scale models. This position can be based remotely anywhere in the U.S. (there may be some restrictions based on legal entity). Please note that this role would not provide relocation as a result. The expectation of working hours and travel (domestic and/or international) will be defined by the hiring manager. This position will require 20% travel. Job Description Key Responsibilities Design and implement intelligent, self-healing data pipelines that leverage AI/ML for automated data quality monitoring, anomaly detection, and remediation. Build and maintain centralized feature stores that enable feature reusability across multiple models and use cases. Create curated data repositories optimized for data science/AI workflows, including training datasets, evaluation datasets, and production serving layers. Develop automated feature engineering pipelines that transform raw data into analytics-ready features with lineage tracking. Partner with Enterprise IT to optimize analytics platform architecture for high-performance data science workloads. Build automated pipelines that integrate diverse data sources including sales, CRM, patient claims, real-world evidence, and unstructured data. Create self-service data access layers that empower data scientists and analysts to query and extract data independently. Establish SLAs for data availability, freshness, and quality; implement monitoring and observability solutions. Essential Requirements Advanced degree in Computer Science, Data Engineering, or related field; 10+ years of experience in data engineering, ML/AI engineering, or analytics infrastructure. 5+ years leading teams building enterprise-scale data platforms and feature stores. Expert knowledge of feature store technologies (Feast, Tecton, SageMaker Feature Store, Databricks Feature Store). Deep expertise in modern data platforms optimized for ML workloads (Databricks, Auto ML, Snowflake, BigQuery). Strong proficiency in Python, SQL, Spark/PySpark for large-scale data processing. Experience with data orchestration tools (Airflow, Prefect, dbt) and CI/CD for data pipelines. Understanding of data governance, privacy (HIPAA, GDPR), and compliance in life sciences. Preferred Qualities Proven track record of implementing AI/ML-powered automation in data engineering workflows. Strategic thinker who can balance innovation (cutting-edge AI tools) with reliability (production stability). Builder mindset with ability to create scalable, self-service capabilities that reduce dependency on data engineering. Experience in pharmaceutical, healthcare, or life sciences industry. Knowledge of streaming technologies, MLOps tools, and data lakehouse architecture. Novartis Compensation Summary: The salary for this position is expected to range between $194,600 and $361,400 per year. The final salary offered is determined based on factors like, but not limited to, relevant skills and experience, and upon joining Novartis will be reviewed periodically. Novartis may change the published salary range based on company and market factors. Your compensation will include a performance-based cash incentive and, depending on the level of the role, eligibility to be considered for annual equity awards. US-based eligible employees will receive a comprehensive benefits package that includes health, life and disability benefits, a 401(k) with company contribution and match, and a variety of other benefits. In addition, employees are eligible for a generous time off package including vacation, personal days, holidays and other leaves EEO Statement: The Novartis Group of Companies are Equal Opportunity Employers. We do not discriminate in recruitment, hiring, training, promotion or other employment practices for reasons of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital or veteran status

title: Junior Managers Program (Trainee) - Start your Leadership Journey in Business Intelligence & Analytics
description: Ready to make a real impact with data? We are looking for analytically strong and tech-savvy master’s graduates with a drive to make a difference, who will drive Bosch's data-driven transformation with us in our Junior Managers Program. If you burn for data analytics, machine learning, and strategic challenges and aspire to build a leadership career, we want to meet you.​ Over an intensive 12 to 24-month journey, you will rotate through predominantly commercial and IT-related departments in Germany and abroad. Your mission is to gain a deep understanding of our business and data-driven decision-making processes, while building expertise in data analytics, digitalization, and machine learning.​ You will analyze complex challenges, identify optimization potentials along our business processes, and collaborate with specialist departments to develop innovative, data-based, digital solutions. description: Bereit, mit Daten echte Wirkung zu erzielen? title: Clinical Operations Specialist (Finance)
description: Business Introduction At GSK, we have bold ambitions for patients, aiming to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade. Our R&D focuses on discovering and delivering vaccines and medicines, combining our understanding of the immune system with cutting-edge technology to transform people’s lives. GSK fosters a culture ambitious for patients, accountable for impact, and committed to doing the right thing, making sure that we focus our efforts on accelerating significant assets that meet patients’ needs and have the highest probability of success. We’re uniting science, technology, and talent to get ahead of disease together. You will play a pivotal role as a member of the local clinical study team and are responsible for contributing to the planning, execution, and delivery of the Clinical trial in the country. This role offers visible career growth, a chance to shape ways of working, and meaningful impact while uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. Responsibilities This role will provide YOU the opportunity to lead key activities to progress YOUR career. These responsibilities include some of the following: Financial analysis, Forecasting and Payments Responsible for tracking and managing the study budget in country once the study budget build is complete. Responsible for ensuring timely and accurate payments to investigator sites/vendors as per the agreed contract. Will set-up, input and manage the payment schedule within dedicated systems. Supports the Local Delivery Lead with regular study budget forecasting activities and reports budget status to internal stakeholders. May act as the business owner and be responsible for oversight of vendor(s) managing investigator site payments. Prepares purchase orders or task orders for services. Ensures compliance to SOPs and upholds integrity of investigator payments to any internal/external audits. Other Clinical Operation Specialist Responsibilities Responsible for coordinating and updating information required for institutional reports and external stakeholders. Could act as subject matter expert at the LOC for different applications applicable to their role. Provide administrative support to the local GMASE department by coordinating meetings, managing communication flows, acting as the liaison between local and global teams, and performing related administrative duties. Leverages AI-enabled tools and digital solutions responsibly to improve efficiency, data quality, and decision-making in clinical trial operations Why You? Working arrangement This role is offered as hybrid working. You will combine remote work with regular time in a UK office and occasional site visits. Basic Qualification We are seeking professionals with the following required skills and qualifications to help us achieve our goals Bachelor’s degree, or equivalent, or relevant experience in clinical operations or similar positions in the pharmaceutical industry. Solid knowledge of ICH-GCP, local regulations, and regulatory processes. Experience with investigator payment systems and purchase order / vendor payment set up and processing. Excellent understanding of the external clinical trial environment and UK clinical trials regulations and start-up processes. Flexible and responsive to new ideas in a changing environment. Preferred Qualification If you have the following characteristics, it would be a plus Enthusiasm for AI-enabled tools and digital solutions to improve efficiency, data quality, and decision-making in clinical trial operations Strong communication skills and relationship management abilities What we value We welcome people from different backgrounds and life experiences. We support an inclusive workplace where everyone can contribute and grow. We look for colleagues who act with integrity, communicate openly and help each other succeed. You will have room to grow your skills, take on responsibility, and make a direct contribution to how we generate evidence. Ready to apply? If you seek to make a difference on a global scale, working with next-gen technologies and the sharpest collaborative teams, then we could be a perfect match. In this role, you will play a central part in evaluating, structuring and executing strategic real estate transactions globally. title: Pflichtpraktikum Zentralcontrolling
description: Du möchtest nicht nur Zahlen verwalten, sondern aktiv die finanzielle Zukunft eines führenden Maschinenbauunternehmens mitgestalten? Bei uns tauchst du tief in die Welt der Unternehmenssteuerung ein und leistest einen direkten Beitrag zu unserem Erfolg. Während deines Praktikums unterstützt du bei der übergreifenden Steuerung unseres gesamten Projektportfolios, von der initialen Wirtschaftlichkeitsrechnung über die laufende Budgetverfolgung bis zur finalen Nachkalkulation. Du arbeitest aktiv bei der jährlichen Unternehmens- und Budgetplanung mit und unterstützt unser Team bei der Erstellung des monatlichen Berichtswesens für die Geschäftsführung. Darüber hinaus wirkst du bei der jährlichen Kalkulation und Analyse unserer internen Verrechnungs- und Stundensätze für Engineering, Montage und Service mit, prüfst Daten auf Plausibilität und visualisierst deine Ergebnisse prägnant. An der Kostenstellen-, Kostenträger- und Profit-Center-Rechnung beteiligst du dich aktiv und trägst dazu bei, die Kostentransparenz im gesamten Unternehmen sicherzustellen. Nicht zuletzt bringst du deine Ideen bei der Analyse und Weiterentwicklung unserer Controlling-Instrumente und -Prozesse ein und arbeitest an abteilungsübergreifenden Sonderthemen mit. Ausbildung: Studium im wirtschaftswissenschaftlichen Bereich wie BWL, Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen, Wirtschaftsinformatik oder vergleichbar mit Schwerpunkt Controlling, Finanzen oder Unternehmensrechnung Erfahrungen und Know-how: sicherer Umgang mit Datenbanken und Excel, auch bei großen Datenmengen; erste theoretische oder praktische Kenntnisse in SAP von Vorteil Persönlichkeit und Arbeitsweise: dir gelingt es, eigenverantwortlich, proaktiv und detailgenau zu arbeiten, wobei du unternehmensweite Zusammenhänge schnell erfasst und analytisch denkst Arbeitsalltag: deine Präsenz vor Ort ist erforderlich Sprachen: verhandlungssicheres Deutsch
description_en: Do you not just want to manage numbers, but also want to actively shape the financial future of a leading mechanical engineering company? With us, you will immerse yourself deeply in the world of corporate management and make a direct contribution to our success. During your internship, you will support the comprehensive management of our entire project portfolio, from the initial profitability calculation to ongoing budget tracking to the final post-calculation. You will actively participate in annual corporate and budget planning and support our team in preparing monthly reports for management. In addition, you will be involved in the annual calculation and analysis of our internal billing and hourly rates for engineering, assembly and service, check data for plausibility and visualize your results concisely. You will actively participate in cost center, cost object and profit center accounting and help ensure cost transparency throughout the company. Last but not least, you will contribute your ideas to the analysis and further development of our controlling instruments and processes and work on cross-departmental special topics. Education: Studies in the field of economics such as business administration, industrial engineering, business informatics or comparable with a focus on controlling, finance or corporate accounting Experience and know-how: confident use of databases and Excel, even with large amounts of data; Initial theoretical or practical knowledge of SAP is an advantage Personality and way of working: you are able to work independently, proactively and with attention to detail, whereby you quickly grasp company-wide connections and think analytically. Day-to-day work: your on-site presence is required. Languages: business-fluent German

title: Head of Global Financial Services
description: Are you looking for a career in an inspiring, global environment where your expertise makes a difference? At Neste, you will be working for the world’s leading producer of renewable diesel and sustainable aviation fuel, which enable our customers to reduce their greenhouse gas emissions. We are looking for you, Head of Global Financial Services to join our Group Finance organization in Neste headquarters in Espoo. You will focus on leading a global shared service center, Neste Global Financial Services (GFS), which is responsible for timely and accurate monthly, quarterly and annual statutory reporting to internal stakeholders, external auditors and authorities. The service scope includes Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Payments, Asset and Inventory Accounting and General Accounting for Neste subsidiaries across Renewable Products and Oil Products business areas. In this job you will work closely with your own highly skilled GFS leadership team, top-tier finance professionals across the Neste Group, and key function and business stakeholders globally. In our team, you will be part of a well-motivated and experienced group of professionals who are driven to continuously improve our processes and develop our talents. As a team, we aim to elevate our financial operations and support Neste's strategic decision-making. Together with your expertise, we can do meaningful work to drive Neste forward. Reasons to join We operate in an inspiring and evolving business environment as a global leader in renewable fuels. We contribute to Neste’s success by living our values every day: we care, we have courage, we cooperate. We prioritize safety at all times and in every location. We strive to create a positive and impactful work environment. Transformation brings new possibilities and fosters our courage and curiosity. As a global company, we support personal development with versatile learning and career opportunities. Collaboration is key, and we believe in flexible, smart ways of working. We work at the office at least three days a week to ensure seamless teamwork and a sense of belonging. In addition, our benefits for employees in Finland include, for example, a personnel fund as part of the overall remuneration, good occupational health care, a membership in a sickness or health insurance fund and leisure time accident insurance. We also support leisure time activities, e.g. by offering benefits for sports and culture (ePassi). More about the job Your role in our team Leading the Global Financial Services department’s overall performance, including heading your own leadership team of 7 direct reports and an organization of 65+ finance professionals based in Espoo, Finland. Ensuring timely and accurate financial reporting while leading robust financial service processes with strong global internal controls. Maintaining and developing the global service delivery model and fostering strong partnerships with key stakeholders and counterparties. Driving end-to-end process development, continuous improvement, and financial service automation. Participating in IT systems renewals and M&A projects to provide all potential new group companies with scalable, proper financial services. Keys to success in this role Applicable education, e.g., Master’s degree in Accounting or Finance, combined with at least 10 years of relevant work experience. Proven track record in leadership, including providing strategic direction, coaching managers, driving team performance, and fostering global collaboration. Expertise in timely/accurate reporting, internal control frameworks, and running cost management. Solid knowledge of financial processes, systems (especially SAP FI), and accounting principles (IAS/IFRS and Local GAAPs). Experience in end-to-end process development, automation methods (e.g., RPA and AI), and participation in finance IT system projects. Proactive and analytical approach, high adaptability to changing situations, and a strong sense of ownership. Excellent communication skills and a collaborative, positive mindset. Let’s get you started We look forward to receiving your CV and application with a salary request by August 31, 2026. Please note that the review of applications will start already during the application period, so submit your application right away! If you have any questions regarding the process or the position, please get in touch with Kaisa Koivuranta, Vice President, Group Finance +358 50 458 4985 on Friday 14
